title_guess: Net domestic product and net national product: depreciation as the gap between gross and net

segments.teaches: the four national income measures; GDP and GNP were covered, NDP and NNP come now

elements.what: cream heading chip: national income
list of four abbreviations with full names
green frame around the first two rows
green ticks on the two rows already covered

segments.notes: Progress checklist used as an opener: ticks mark what earlier videos covered.

segments.teaches: gross measures give the total value; net measures give what remains after deductions

elements.what: left cream panel with the two gross measures (green frame, ticks)
right cream panel with the two net measures (blue frame)
labels under each panel on a dark rule: gross value / net value
small pointer boxes: 'total value' under gross, 'value left after deductions' under net

segments.notes: The checklist rows physically regroup into two side-by-side panels.

segments.teaches: farm example: seeds worth 10 grow wheat worth 100; gross produce 100, net produce 90

elements.what: farmer sowing seeds
sack of wheat
arrow from seeds (price in red) to wheat (price in green)
blue chips gross produce and net produce with values written beside them

segments.notes: Running numeric example with small round numbers (10 in, 100 out, 90 net). Input cost in red, output in green.

segments.teaches: a machine is a depreciating asset: its value falls every year until it is worthless; the government sets depreciation rates

elements.what: factory production line feeding into a sauce bottle
heading 'machine' with a red tag of the yearly depreciation percentage added later
red bracketed label: depreciating asset
blue chips gross produce / net produce on the right
value (starting at 1 crore) vs year; a dotted arrow curves down from the start year to zero at a year twenty years later
info card with a government icon and a blue side bar: depreciation rates are notified by a ministry
national emblem inside the government icon

segments.notes: The decay curve draws itself in two stages (short arrow, then extended to zero). National emblem should not be reused.

segments.teaches: depreciation is booked as an expense; value falls from 1 crore to 70 lakh, a 30 lakh expense that can wipe out a 25 lakh profit, so no tax

elements.what: blue two-row year/value table: start year 1 crore, next year 70 lakh (new value in red)
dotted curved arrow from the table to a pink depreciation (expense) card showing 30 lakh
green year/profit card showing 25 lakh, placed beside the expense card
thick grey frame grouping profit and expense
arrow from the frame to a bold 'no tax' label

segments.notes: Running numeric example continues (1 crore -> 70 lakh -> 30 lakh expense vs 25 lakh profit). The graph is swapped for the number table in the same slot.

segments.teaches: the machine makes 10 lakh bottles at 10 each: gross produce 1 crore, net produce 1 crore minus 30 lakh depreciation

elements.what: pink depreciation card moved up under the machine
teal elbow connector from the expense card to the government info card
unit price under the bottle and a 'times 10 lakh' multiplier beside it
beside the chips: gross produce = 1 crore; net produce = 1 crore minus 30 lakh (deduction in red)

segments.notes: Ties the running numbers back to the gross/net chips that were waiting empty since the start of the machine scene.

elements.what: the gross and net panels from earlier, brought back
big curved arc from gross value down and up to net value, labelled 'minus depreciation' in red

segments.notes: Recall of the earlier composition, now with the missing link drawn as an arc.

segments.teaches: GDP minus depreciation = NDP; GNP minus depreciation = NNP; depreciation counts only assets used for production

elements.what: two stacked equations with the shared depreciation term in a cream column, red text
pointer box above the depreciation column: only assets businesses use to produce goods
mobile phone labelled used for business purpose, with a dotted arrow

segments.notes: Equations are aligned so the common term forms one highlighted column. Everyday-object example (phone) for the business-use rule.

segments.teaches: recap: three measures now covered, NNP next

elements.what: the four-row list again, three rows on green bands
green ticks on the three covered rows

segments.notes: Same checklist as the opener, one more tick: a progress bookend.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels
